disagreements.subject: the probe lane's kill of S1, cubic theta with the conjugate cubic twist (k = 3)
disagreements.kill_as_described_in_the_task: leaves the angular factor alpha-bar(c), so that the denominator is L(s, eta alpha-bar)
disagreements.referee_finding: gamma_2 gamma_4 = 1 exactly at norm 7 and at the two-prime indices 7 and (1+3w)(4+3w): no Moebius sign and no cross phase. With the paper's row normalization the u = 1 coefficient of X = Q^{-x} is +conj(alpha(p) G(p)) eta rho^{-4}, so an angular factor (together with conj(G(p))) does appear. With a bare row (no angular, G or R insertion, each of which exists to cancel phases produced by gamma_1 gamma_2 = mu alpha G and absent here) it is exactly +eta rho^{-4}, and the local factor at norms 7 and 13 factors as (1-V)^{-1} (1-W)^{-1} (1 - eta^2 X^2)(1 - eta X)^{-1} H with no pure X or X^2 in H - 1. The target enters as L(x, eta)/L(2x, eta^2): in the numerator, not the denominator, and the angular factor is removable.
points_of_disagreement: exponent of the target: numerator (+1), not denominator
the angular factor is an artifact of the paper's row normalization, not forced by the probe
disagreements.agreement: a factorization with 1/L(x, eta), the shape the zero detector needs, is absent; the kill's conclusion stands for a different reason
disagreements.caveat: The referee's S1 is its own construction from the task's one-line description; the lane's definition was not read. The disagreement may be one of definitions rather than of mathematics.

consistent_with_the_task_descriptions.subject: S2, the quadratic twist (k = 2): said to have no scalar Euler identity
consistent_with_the_task_descriptions.referee_finding: At norm 7 the X coefficient has alpha-exponent 1/3 (bare row), -2/3 (paper's row normalization) and -1/3 (conjugate theta). Since gamma_2^3 = -alpha(p) and alpha(p) is not a root of unity, no finite-ray phase or integer power of alpha makes it scalar. The attempt to exhibit a scalar identity failed.

consistent_with_the_task_descriptions.subject: S3, classical theta with a quartic twist: said to lack squarefree coefficients
consistent_with_the_task_descriptions.referee_finding: Over Q(i), at the prime -1+2i of norm 5 by direct summation through t = 4 and at 3+2i of norm 13: theta coefficients 2, 0, 2, 0, 2 at p^t, so no X term in any row; the non-scalar twist values (quartic Gauss sums, alpha-exponent 1/2 and -1/2) sit only at odd t where the theta vanishes; every surviving coefficient is scalar and the u = 1 row starts at X^4. Consistent; in addition, a scalar local factor does exist, in Q^{-2x} and Q^{-4x}, which no zero detector at abscissa x can use.
consistent_with_the_task_descriptions.grade: derived at norms 5 and 13 of Z[i]
